items.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
items.summary: The paper introduces JDPI, using contrastive prototypes to detect jailbreaks in LLMs without extra classifiers.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a lightweight, potentially more robust safety check for deploying safer language models.

items.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
items.summary: The paper proposes a trait theory linking reviewer value in human-AI collaboration to metacognitive calibration, the match between confidence and accuracy.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this can improve AI-human decision quality by selecting reviewers who best complement AI.

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.summary: The article maps the AI supply chain, detailing how various organizations contribute models, data, compute, capital, and talent, and highlights gaps in documenting interconnections.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding these links helps tech leaders spot bottlenecks, assess risks, and guide investment in AI infrastructure.

items.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
items.summary: The article discusses a new beta approach to agentic harness engineering that focuses on evolving harnesses based on explicit and implicit user requirements.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should know it improves AI system adaptability and reduces narrow, ineffective updates.

items.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
items.summary: The paper analyzes how SGD dynamics in two-layer neural networks split into teacher-aligned signal and orthogonal noise, affecting generalization.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this split helps tech-savvy readers design better training regimes and diagnose overfitting.

items.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
items.summary: The paper introduces a framework using minimal homogeneous generators to build equivariant polynomial features for learning functions between group representations.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers benefit from a unified, efficient method for designing symmetry-aware models across domains.

items.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
items.summary: The article examines how to evaluate user simulators for interactive agents, questioning whether current frameworks detect meaningful failures and what high benchmark scores truly indicate.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding simulator reliability is crucial for developing robust AI agents that perform well with real users.

items.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
items.summary: Cap-and-Track optimizes LLM inference dispatch by adapting to changing fleet capacity and variable request sizes, using asynchronous handling across providers and GPUs.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it improves efficiency and reliability of large‑model services amid dynamic resource availability.

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.summary: The article introduces the Personal Imitation Game, testing if LLMs can mimic a specific individual’s conversational style, using 30 participants and stylometric cues.
items.whyItMatters: It highlights limits of LLMs in personalized identity replication, relevant for privacy and AI authenticity concerns.

items.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
items.summary: The paper presents CAR, an AI framework that grounds research ideas in literature, iteratively refines them, and uses explicit operators to generate novel proposals.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a systematic way to automate scientific ideation, potentially accelerating discovery for tech researchers.

items.title: Monoculture Robust Learning
items.summary: The paper defines monoculture robustness in PAC learning to reduce shared failure modes among models using the same data.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it promises more reliable, diverse AI systems that avoid collective blind spots.

items.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
items.summary: The article discusses using local AI agents to automate power electronics simulation loops, reducing manual design iterations.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it speeds up design, cuts cloud costs, and enables on-premise inference.

items.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
items.summary: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs…

items.title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision
items.summary: Neural PDE operators are often optimized through state reconstruction, which largely constrains operator values at observed inputs but does not fully characterize their sensitivity to local perturbations. items.summary: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. items.summary: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops. items.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible. items.summary: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills. items.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
items.summary: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes.
